newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices lifted by cold front.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices lifted by cold front.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly higher again Thursday as colder weather kept heating demand high.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be about three to 15 degrees below-normal through the middle of next week, the National Weather Service reported.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Friday were in the $24.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, up from Wednesday's range of $22.00-23.00.
However, firm, peak prices into TVA were talked as low as $20.00 per MWh.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in northern TVA for Friday were assessed at $14.00-15.00, traders said.

As cold temperatures moved into the area, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks at the Georgia/Florida border for Friday delivery were stronger in the $24.00-25.00 range, as compared with Wednesday's $22.50-23.50 range.
For 12-hour scheduling, firm peak prices at the border were talked in the $27.00-28.00 per MWh range, with offers heard as high as $30.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally at $13.00-14.00.
Firm, peak prices in Florida were talked in the $25.00-26.00 range, though most buyers were purchasing power on an hourly basis as they watched the changing weather patterns.
